question: For an unbiased random-feature representation of a positive-definite kernel, what importance-sampling distribution minimizes expected one-sample approximation variance, and when does that optimum cease to depend on the chosen feature representation?

key_findings.claim: The variance-minimizing proposal samples a feature parameter in proportion to its base density times the geometric mean of its second moments under the two input distributions.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 derives p_Psi(omega) proportional to p_Omega(omega) q_phi(omega), where q_phi is the square root of E_{X1}[phi(x1,omega)^2] times E_{X2}[phi(x2,omega)^2]. The result follows by rewriting the expected second moment as an integral of p_Omega^2 q_phi^2 / p_Psi and solving its constrained minimization with a Lagrange multiplier.

key_findings.claim: At that proposal, the exact expected variance is the squared base-measure expectation of q_phi minus the expected squared kernel value.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 states V_hat = (E_{omega~Omega} q_phi(omega))^2 - E_{x1~X1,x2~X2} K(x1,x2)^2. The proof isolates the kernel-squared term, which is proposal-independent, and minimizes the remaining second moment.

key_findings.claim: Representation-independent equality is proved only when the two kernel arguments share the same marginal input distribution; otherwise the paper gives a common upper bound, not equality across representations.
key_findings.evidence: Corollary 1 bounds the optimal variance by E[K(x1,x1)K(x2,x2)-K(x1,x2)^2] using Cauchy-Schwarz, which removes phi but may be loose. Corollary 2 turns that bound into equality only under X1 = X2, because q_phi then reduces to the same second moment on both sides. The title and abstract omit this condition and therefore read more broadly than the theorem supports.

anchors.section: 4. The Choice of Feature Representation Does Not Matter, Corollaries 1-2

key_findings.claim: The theoretically optimal sampler is data- and representation-dependent even in the regime where its achieved variance is representation-independent.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 2 defines the objective by expectations over X1 and X2, and the optimal density contains q_phi, which itself requires representation-specific second moments over those distributions. The equality result concerns the value of the optimum, not a single universal proposal distribution shared by all feature maps.

key_findings.claim: The paper establishes an oracle variance result but provides no implementable estimator or empirical evidence that approximating the oracle improves kernel regression or attention.
key_findings.evidence: After the proof and two corollaries, the paper ends with references. It contains no algorithm for estimating q_phi, no treatment of proposal sampling or weights when q_phi is known only approximately, no finite-data generalization analysis, and no experiments on pointwise kernels, KNNs, attention, or downstream tasks.

anchors.section: Corollary 2 and end of main text

method.core_idea: Hold the random-feature identity for a kernel fixed but change the sampling measure through importance weights, then solve directly for the proposal that minimizes expected per-sample mean-squared error over two input distributions.
method.mechanism: Rewrite K(x1,x2)=E_Omega[phi(x1,omega)phi(x2,omega)] as an expectation under a same-support proposal Psi with likelihood ratio p_Omega/p_Psi. Expand variance into a proposal-dependent second moment and a fixed squared mean. Average the former over X1 and X2, factor it using independence into representation-specific second moments q_phi, and use constrained variational/Lagrange optimization to obtain p_Psi proportional to p_Omega q_phi. Cauchy-Schwarz yields a representation-free upper bound; identical input marginals make it tight.
assumptions: The kernel is positive definite and admits the stated symmetric scalar random-feature representation.
The proposal and base distributions possess densities and the proposal has the same support as the base measure.
The two input arguments are independently drawn from specified marginal distributions X1 and X2 so the second moments factor.
All required second moments and normalization constants are finite.
The application objective is expected per-sample kernel-estimation variance, rather than worst-case error, downstream loss, numerical stability, or total computation.
For the strongest equivalence statement, X1 and X2 are the same distribution.

techniques.role: Changes which feature parameters are sampled while preserving the unbiased kernel expectation through a density ratio.
Aggregates one-sample approximation variance over application-specific input marginals.
Solves analytically for the normalized proposal density that minimizes the expected second moment.
Removes the feature map from an upper bound and identifies the identical-marginal condition under which the bound is exact.

evaluations.setting: Any positive-definite kernel with a scalar symmetric unbiased random-feature representation and independent inputs from X1 and X2
evaluations.metric: Expected one-sample variance over the input marginals
evaluations.result: Theorem 1 gives the global minimizing proposal p_Psi proportional to p_Omega q_phi and its exact attained variance.
evaluations.baseline: Naive sampling from the base feature distribution Omega

evaluations.result: Corollary 2 makes the representation-free Cauchy-Schwarz upper bound exact, so all admissible scalar representations have the same optimum value.
evaluations.baseline: All other random-feature representations under their own oracle-optimal proposal

limitations: The equality across feature representations requires X1 = X2; for cross-distribution kernels the paper proves only a shared upper bound.
The proposal depends on q_phi, an expectation over the unknown or potentially changing application data distribution, and the paper gives no estimator for it.
There are no experiments, numerical examples, pseudocode, approximation guarantees for learned proposals, or wall-clock comparisons.
The analysis is per-sample and does not cover correlated feature sets such as orthogonal or simplex couplings, whose multi-sample covariance is central to competing methods.
The objective ignores numerical stability, positivity, memory layout, feature-computation cost, normalization bias in linear attention, and downstream-task error.
Same support and density-ratio assumptions can fail or become unstable when the optimal mass concentrates in rare regions of the base measure.
The prose says the variance is the mean-squared error without separately discussing bias introduced by a finite-data approximation to the proposal or self-normalized importance sampling.
failure_modes: Estimating q_phi from a small dataset can overfit the proposal to observed inputs and worsen error on shifted queries or keys.
A highly concentrated optimal density can produce difficult sampling, large likelihood ratios under approximation error, or poor coverage of rare but important input pairs.
In cross-attention or retrieval, query and key marginals differ, so feature-representation dependence can remain through the looseness of Corollary 1.
For a finite feature bank with correlated samples, independently drawing from the one-sample optimal density need not minimize total estimator variance.
Choosing a computationally expensive representation remains harmful even if its oracle sample variance matches a cheaper one; variance equivalence is not systems equivalence.
Nonstationary attention distributions would require tracking q_phi during training or inference, potentially erasing the linear-attention speed advantage.
reusable_insights: Separate representation design from sampling design: apparent gains from a feature map can vanish when every representation is evaluated under its own optimized proposal.
State equivalence conditions at the same prominence as the equivalence claim; a representation-free upper bound is not a representation-free optimum unless tightness is established.
Oracle results should identify the information needed to instantiate the oracle, here representation-specific second moments over deployment inputs.
When a theorem optimizes expected approximation error, a practical follow-up should measure the statistical and computational cost of estimating the optimizing distribution.
Input-distribution asymmetry is a natural stress test for results derived under interchangeable kernel arguments, especially for cross-attention and retrieval.
open_questions: Can q_phi and its normalizer be estimated online with a provable regret or variance bound under drifting query/key distributions?
How does an approximate proposal's error translate into excess variance relative to the oracle, and is that bound stable under importance-weight clipping?
What is the jointly optimal distribution for a correlated bank of m features rather than a single independent feature?
Does representation equivalence survive asymmetric query and key distributions, vector-valued feature maps, causal masks, or normalized softmax attention?
When feature evaluation and proposal-sampling costs are included, which representation minimizes error per unit time or memory despite equal oracle sample variance?
Can empirical evaluations reproduce FAVOR# and SimRF gains after giving their alternative feature maps and standard maps equally strong learned importance proposals?

competitive_landscape.title: Rethinking Attention with Performers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational positive-random-feature application to linear-time softmax attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Performer chooses a numerically stable positive feature representation and deploys it as FAVOR+ in end-to-end attention, including practical guarantees and task evaluations. The equivalence paper instead optimizes the sampling density for an arbitrary scalar representation, but does not address normalized attention, causal computation, or an implementable proposal.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2021 oral forum, current record checked 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: FAVOR#: Sharp Attention Kernel Approximations via New Classes of Positive Random Features
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct representation-optimization target of the paper's claimed random-feature arms race
competitive_landscape.difference: FAVOR# parameterizes positive nontrigonometric representations, derives closed-form variance-reducing parameters, and reports very large pointwise variance reductions plus kernel-regression, speech, and NLP gains. The equivalence theorem says representation-level variance advantages disappear under each representation's oracle importance proposal only in its stated expected-variance regime, but offers no empirical test of that prediction.

competitive_landscape.title: Simplex Random Features
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing variance optimum obtained through correlations among multiple random features
competitive_landscape.difference: SimRF geometrically couples an m-feature set and proves optimality within weight-independent positive-feature couplings, with an asymptotic broader result for SimRF+, then evaluates pointwise kernels, classification, and Transformers. The equivalence paper optimizes the marginal proposal for one feature and does not model cross-feature covariance, so it does not subsume Simplex's multi-sample optimality claim.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Directly minimizing variance over importance-sampling distributions yields a global optimum whose error is independent of the random-feature representation, ending the need to design ever better representations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Theorem 1 supplies the proposal and exact objective value; Corollary 1 supplies a representation-free upper bound; Corollary 2 proves equality across representations when X1 equals X2.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The clean oracle derivation is useful and the identical-marginal equality is a sharp conceptual result. Its scope is materially narrower than the title: it does not prove equality for asymmetric inputs, correlated finite feature banks, approximate/data-limited proposal estimation, systems cost, or downstream attention. Those gaps also keep Performer, FAVOR#, and Simplex Random Features directly competitive rather than rendered obsolete.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete five-page v2 extraction, including the proof and references. The record distinguishes the theorem's exact identical-marginal result from its general upper bound. Primary-source versions were checked on arXiv, OpenReview, and PMLR on 2026-08-23; OpenReview's public forum was challenge-gated at check time, so the forum identity/venue was cross-checked against the paper's own reference and search metadata.
